title: How to Jump-Start a Stale, Boring Classroom
author: Michael Linsin
summary: Written for the midyear slump when routine breeds student disengagement, Linsin runs through quick novelty tactics (new seating, outdoor lessons, learning games, more urgency and humor) before identifying one strategy he considers uniquely powerful: what he calls 'detailed modeling.' His claim is that most teachers model far less than needed, and that the real breakthrough isn't modeling more often but modeling with exacting, granular detail -- demonstrating not just the end behavior but every small physical and cognitive step involved, such as sitting at a desk, listening for a signal, collecting materials, and narrating the thinking process aloud. He argues that this level of detail is interesting to students in its own right because it lets them visualize themselves succeeding, and that it functions as an antidote to boredom specifically because it constantly supplies fresh, concrete goals rather than vague expectations. He notes the technique isn't limited to serious procedures -- teachers can add playful or even nonsensical steps to make modeling more memorable -- while stressing it still produces a well-choreographed, if relaxed-looking, classroom.
points: Most teachers under-model; the fix isn't modeling more often alone but modeling with exacting, granular physical and cognitive detail.
Detailed modeling means narrating and acting out even minor steps -- sitting down, listening for a signal, collecting materials -- not just describing the end goal.
This level of detail works as a boredom antidote because it gives students a constant, concrete succession of visible goals rather than vague expectations.
Modeling doesn't have to be rigid or militaristic -- adding playful or nonsensical steps can make it more memorable while the underlying structure stays well choreographed.
quotes: Every day feels like the one before and motivation ratchets downward. Some simple things you can do to help reverse the trend include:
The first step is to model more frequently. The truth is, few teachers model enough. Most come nowhere near the amount needed to significantly improve student performance.
However, what really pulls them in is to add exacting and explicit detail. Very few teachers do this, but it’s remarkably effective.
Within each of theses movements you would be even more detailed, acting out your facial expressions and explaining your thinking process. You’re essentially providing a mental-visual map to success.
This doesn’t mean militaristic. Your class can appear as relaxed as you choose, but underneath it’s well choreographed.
Most importantly, especially for this time of year, it’s a powerful antidote to boredom. Of course, you don’t have to model already proven and well-performed routines.
